subject: Decision Making
subcategory: Famous Decisions That Changed the World
title: Kennedy Chooses the Moon
description: One-minute skill: Kennedy Chooses the Moon.

hook.text: In 1961, Kennedy declared America would reach the moon by decade's end. NASA had barely put a man in orbit.

buildup.text: The Soviets were winning the space race. Kennedy needed a goal so ambitious it would redefine the competition.

discovery.text: The decision was political, not scientific. Kennedy chose the moon because it was far enough away that both nations.

twist.text: Kennedy privately asked advisors if the US could beat the Soviets. They said only on a moon landing, nothing closer.

climax.text: Kennedy chose a deadline that forced innovation. Constraints create urgency, and urgency drives breakthroughs.

punchline.text: Barely in orbit, aiming for the moon. Bold deadlines forced innovation.

quiz.question: Why did Kennedy specifically choose the moon?
options: It was far enough that the US and USSR started on equal footing
